corners.name: T1

corners.name: T2
corners.tip: Slow in, fast out: do all your braking in a straight line, turn in late, apex late, then get to full throttle as early as the exit allows.

corners.name: T3
corners.tip: Trail brake toward the apex, aim for a slightly late apex, and use all the road on exit so you can open the steering and throttle early.

corners.name: T4
corners.tip: Carry momentum: brake lightly or just lift, use one smooth steering input, and let the car run to the outside on exit. Over-slowing here costs a lot.

corners.name: T5

pros.title: You commit to the brake pedal in 3 of 5 braking zones

pros.title: 62.5% of the lap at full throttle

pros.title: Very few locked wheels

cons.detail: About 55 m per lap in T4. You come off the brake, roll, and only then pick up the throttle. The car is slowing with nothing controlling its balance, so you lose time and the front goes light before the apex.

cons.title: Rear wheelspin on exit in 3 corners

cons.title: Brake released abruptly while turning (T1, T5)

cons.title: Running wide of the apex (T1)

cons.title: Busy hands: steering corrections mid-corner (T1, T4)
cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Not using all the road on exit (T1)
cons.detail: T1: about 5.3 m more was available. Using the full width lets you straighten the wheel and get on the throttle sooner.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T2, T1
cons.detail: T2: 0.66 s between your average and best pass; T1: 0.16 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T4.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit 90-100% immediately at high speed, then progressively release as the car slows. A formula car loses downforce as it slows, so the same pedal pressure that was fine at 280 km/h locks the wheels at 120 km/h.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins. Consider turning traction control on while you learn.

improve.title: Hit the apex
improve.target: Within 0.5 m of your best line at every apex
improve.how: In T1, turn in slightly later and aim the car at the inside kerb. If you still can't reach it, you're carrying too much speed in: brake a touch more.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Snapping off the brake with the wheel turned
stopDoing.detail: Release it gradually over the last 20-30 m before the apex.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

cons.detail: Repeated small corrections mean the car is moving around under you or the line needs adjusting mid-corner. Both cost speed.

cons.title: Not using all the road on exit (T3, T4)
cons.detail: T3: about 2.5 m more was available; T4: about 2.4 m more was available. Using the full width lets you straighten the wheel and get on the throttle sooner.

cons.title: Inconsistent through T2, T4, T5
cons.detail: T2: 0.40 s between your average and best pass; T4: 0.35 s between your average and best pass; T5: 0.19 s between your average and best pass.

improve.title: Connect the brake to the throttle
improve.target: Coasting under 8% of the lap, and under 10 m in any corner
improve.how: Keep 10-20% brake on as you turn in and hold it until the slowest point, then go straight to a light throttle. No gap between the pedals. Practice only this for 5 laps, starting with T5, T4.

improve.title: Threshold braking: hard first, then bleed off
improve.target: ABS active less than 20% of each braking zone
improve.how: Hit 90-100% immediately at high speed, then progressively release as the car slows. A formula car loses downforce as it slows, so the same pedal pressure that was fine at 280 km/h locks the wheels at 120 km/h.

improve.title: Squeeze the throttle on exits
improve.target: Rear tyres within ~10°C of the fronts; no wheelspin flags
improve.how: In slow corners take about a second to go from 0 to 100% throttle, and only go to full once the steering is unwinding. Short-shift (change up early) out of hairpins.

improve.title: Hit the apex
improve.target: Within 0.5 m of your best line at every apex
improve.how: In T4, turn in slightly later and aim the car at the inside kerb. If you still can't reach it, you're carrying too much speed in: brake a touch more.

stopDoing.title: Letting go of both pedals between braking and the apex
stopDoing.detail: Every metre without a pedal is time you are not using.

stopDoing.title: Holding the brake pedal flat and letting ABS do the work
stopDoing.detail: Ease off as soon as you feel ABS chatter or see the ABS light.

stopDoing.title: Going to full throttle while the car is still turning
stopDoing.detail: Add throttle as you take steering lock off, not before.

stopDoing.title: Stabbing the throttle and lifting again
stopDoing.detail: Pick it up once, gently, and only ever add more.

stopDoing.title: Snapping off the brake with the wheel turned
stopDoing.detail: Release it gradually over the last 20-30 m before the apex.

stopDoing.title: Sawing at the wheel
stopDoing.detail: One smooth turn in, hold, one smooth unwind. If you need to correct, the input before it was too sudden or too early.

show.item: Live delta to your best lap
show.why: The single most useful number. It turns green/red within a corner, so you instantly know whether a change you just tried worked.
Keep these on while you fix coasting (26.5% now): you'll see the gap between the red and green bars. Remove once it's under 8%.
Your ES wheel already has RPM LEDs, so you don't need to look at the HUD for shifts. Keep the gear number visible.

show.item: Last lap and best lap times
show.why: Glance on the main straight only.
Cold formula tyres lock and spin easily. Check them on the out-lap and after a slide, on straights only.
Formula cars expect you to adjust these during a lap. Only look at them on straights.

hide.item: Full standings / timing tower in practice
hide.why: Irrelevant when you are learning. Use the relative (gap to cars around you) only in races.
Useful for your first laps on a new track. After that, learn the track by real reference points instead.
Never read numbers in a corner. Look through the corner to the apex and exit; read the HUD only on straights.
Only matter in long races. Hide them in practice to reduce clutter.

settings: Steering lock: formula cars use much less rotation than road or GT cars (roughly 360-540°). Let AMS2 set the soft lock for the car, and keep the in-game rotation matched to Pit House so the on-screen wheel turns exactly as far as yours.

Force feedback: high-downforce cars produce big forces in fast corners, so clipping is likely on a 5.5 Nm R5. Turn on AMS2's FFB HUD meter and lower in-game gain until the bar only touches the top briefly.
Keep damping and inertia low in Pit House (as in your R5-AMS2-Claude preset). Formula steering should feel quick and light at low speed.
Learn with brake bias slightly rearward of where it locks the fronts, and ABS/TC on if the car allows it; turn them off later.
